title: Dock single-scalar morph — one spring, one clock, the whole box

The View-Transitions COLLAPSE fork is RETIRED; the route-morph view-transition-name seam is PRESERVED.

sotaFolds.propertyRegistered: --dock-morph-t is @property-registered { syntax: '<number>'; initial-value: 0 } so it interpolates COMPOSITED, not discretely. inherits:true (NOT false) — the bomb guard is specifically 'never write to :root'; the scalar is written on the small .glass-dock subtree and its consumers (.dock-layers/.dock-layer-stack size + the child stagger) are DESCENDANTS that read it via inheritance, so it MUST inherit (the same pattern the prior --dock-morph-progress used on .dock-layers). Recorded as a deliberate divergence from the spec's literal inherits:false.
sotaFolds.squircleRidesTheClock: the shape-card border-radius now MORPHS pill↔card-radius on the same --dock-expand-t scalar; the @supports (corner-shape: squircle) enhancement is unchanged (the arc is the contract, the squircle the better tier).
sotaFolds.noInterpolateSize: no interpolate-size/calc-size on the morph axis — the FLIP from→to px is a one-time MEASUREMENT primitive read once, never a co-driver on the spring's axis.
sotaFolds.velocityContinuity: the live SpringProgress is re-based onto the new span from its current velocity on a re-toggle (reset(0, inheritedVelocity) + target=1), so an interrupted morph carries inertia rather than snapping from rest — the one load-bearing iOS-feel piece CSS linear()/transition + VT cannot do.
